newsitem.title: UK: Goldman denies trader fired after metals turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Goldman denies trader fired after metals turmoil.

text.p: US investment bank Goldman Sachs has denied a British Sunday newspaper report that one of its top metals traders, Thomas Wilson, was fired this week following general turmoil and losses in the metals market.
A spokesman for Goldman said the front page Sunday Telegraph report was "ludicrous."

"No copper trader has resigned or been dismissed and we have had no recent losses in our copper trading," he told Reuters. "This has been a good year for Goldman Sachs in the base metals market generally, including copper."
He confirmed that one Goldman metals trader had indeed left the firm in the last week "by mutual consent and for reasons that have nothing to do with trading losses."
The newspaper report also suggested that Chris Carrera, a managing director, had been brought to London to take over market operations.
"In fact, he has been here for several months, charged with beefing up the metals operation, which shows Goldman's comitment to the sector," the spokesman said.
